findings.claim: Multipart filename values are not redacted before the replay record is saved; only field payloads are processed.
findings.recommended_action: Pass the multipart part head through _redact_text before reassembly, or explicitly parse and redact the filename= parameter in _redact_multipart.
findings.why: [panel:arkcli] [arkcli:kimi-k2.7-code] The function splits each part into head (containing Content-Disposition with filename=...) and payload, then runs _redact_text only on the payload. The head string is appended unchanged, so a non-neutral filename allowed under an auth exception would persist verbatim in replay artifacts, contradicting the report's claim that multipart names/content are redacted.

findings.claim: URL userinfo (https://user:password@host/) bypasses both request validation and replay URL redaction.
findings.recommended_action: Inspect parsed.username and parsed.password in both validate_outbound_request and redact_url, treat them as sensitive auth material, and redact them in saved replay URLs.
findings.why: [panel:arkcli] [arkcli:kimi-k2.7-code] Both functions parse the URL with urlsplit but only inspect parsed.path, parsed.query, and the whole parsed.netloc. Credentials embedded in the URL netloc would pass validation and be stored unredacted in replay records, undermining the header redaction shown in E-004.

findings.claim: sanitize_request_record does not redact response body content, so target-returned secrets or PII may persist in replay snippets.
findings.recommended_action: Extend sanitize_request_record (or the caller that writes response.snippet) to redact response bodies using the same redact_body/_redact_text pipeline applied to requests.
findings.why: [panel:arkcli] [arkcli:kimi-k2.7-code] The function only sanitizes request URL/headers/body plus response Set-Cookie. The response snippet in E-004 is stored verbatim, so a target response echoing a token or PII would be retained in the replay artifact.

findings.claim: tools/exploit.py and tools/sensors/client_graybox.py are absent from the diff and no evidence shows they call the privacy validator.
findings.recommended_action: Either add outbound privacy validation calls to these tools, or explicitly document them as handoff-only/out-of-scope in the audit trail and link that decision to a coverage ledger entry.
findings.why: [panel:arkcli] [arkcli:kimi-k2.7-code] Although the report acknowledges URL-hidden custom scripts are author-and-handoff, these are framework-shipped network tools. Without diff coverage or an explicit handoff-only classification, there is an unverified surface that could emit target-facing bytes without validation.

findings.claim: **`_LOCAL_PATH_RE` creates false-positive risk for legitimate target payloads**
findings.why: [panel:claude] The regex `(?:/Users/[^/\s]+|/home/[^/\s]+|[A-Za-z]:\\Users\\[^\\\s]+)` will block any request body/path/query whose content resembles a Unix/Windows user directory path — even when that content is a legitimate target API parameter (e.g., `{"backup_path": "/Users/shared/data"}`). The disposition PR-003 only addresses the "xunji" literal token case; this broader path-pattern false-positive class is unaddressed. Unlike the hostname exemption, there is no documented override or emergency bypass for legitimate payloads that coincidentally match. | Affected EIDs: E-001

findings.claim: **All confirmed evidence artifacts are loopback-only; proxy path (production default) has zero coverage**
findings.why: [panel:claude] Every confirmed artifact targets `http://127.0.0.1:PORT/`. CLAUDE.md declares `XUNJI_PROXY` as the default egress path with proxy fail-closed behavior. Zero artifacts exercise the privacy guard through the proxy path. The proxy could rewrite URLs, inject headers, alter multipart boundaries, or modify Content-Type in ways unseen by loopback-only selftests. PR-010/final flagged this; the disposition (line 147-149) only adds documentation about trust boundaries without adding proxy-path artifact coverage. | Affected EIDs: E-004, E-005, E-006

findings.claim: **E-004 confirms redaction mechanism but lacks the "fresh guarded replication" that report claim 5 itself requires**
findings.evidence: `privacy-replay-sample.txt.replay.json` (single redacted sample), `privacy-replay-verdict.txt` (SKIPPED-PRIVACY-REDACTED verdict), `report.md:line-20` ("final confirmed evidence requires a per-entry replay disposition and fresh guarded replication")
findings.why: [panel:claude] E-004 proves that Cookie/Set-Cookie are hash-redacted and replay returns `SKIPPED-PRIVACY-REDACTED`. But report claim 5 explicitly requires "fresh guarded replication" plus "per-entry replay disposition" for final confirmed evidence. The bundle contains no second replay artifact showing a re-acquired session was then used to successfully replicate the original request. The round-3 disposition (line 143-145) acknowledges this: "E-004 confirms replay redaction/non-replay semantics only; it does not claim to satisfy fresh authenticated replication for a real vulnerability finding." This is an honest scope admission, but it means claim 5 as written is not fully evidenced. | Affected EIDs: E-004

findings.claim: **Agent template privacy instructions are prose-only defense; report claim 1 scope exceeds hard enforcement**
findings.evidence: `reviewed.diff` (7 agent template files: code-audit.md, exploit.md, report.md, review.md, surface.md, synthesizer.md, verify.md — each adds one prose line), `report.md:claim-1` ("Root and every Agent must keep generated project/run/Agent/operator identity...out of outbound"), `privacy.py.txt:_INTERNAL_PATTERNS` (hard enforcement only at framework-tool layer)
findings.why: [panel:claude] The hooks + guard.py provide hard per-request enforcement for guarded framework tools (probe, render, scan, sensors). But the 7 agent templates only add advisory prose — agents under context pressure, during creative exploit generation, or after future template drift could still emit project-identifying bytes. Report claim 1 uses "must" language implying enforcement, but for agents it's an instruction, not a gate. The round-3 PR-014 disposition (line 137-138) correctly narrows the claim scope, but the report.md text was not updated to reflect this distinction. | Affected EIDs: E-001

findings.claim: **Cross-layer concurrent failure of privacy module is untested**
findings.evidence: `safety_gate.py` selftest hunk (only simulates hook-level privacymod=None), `guard.py` RequestRecorder importing privacy helpers, `disposition.md:line-152-156` (PR-015 recorded as residual — admitted no dual-failure artifact exists)
findings.why: [panel:claude] The hook-level selftest simulates `privacymod = None` and verifies fail-closed for CLI commands. But `guard.py`'s `RequestRecorder` also imports privacy helpers. No test proves both layers fail closed simultaneously. If privacy.py is importable by the hook but unimportable by guard.py (e.g., partial filesystem corruption, different Python paths, conditional imports), enforcement would be inconsistent — commands could pass the hook while per-request checks fail, or vice versa. Disposition acknowledges this as an accepted residual risk without artifact. | Affected EIDs: E-001, E-002

findings.claim: **E-005 artifact self-description contradicts its certainty grade** (residual documentation issue)
findings.evidence: `upload-result.json:30` (`"replicated": "Repeat with a fresh marker before certainty >=0.8."`), `upload-result-2.json:30` (same text)
findings.why: [panel:claude] Both upload result artifacts contain a template string saying "Repeat with a fresh marker before certainty >=0.8." This text was the basis for the prior PR-006 BLOCKER. The replication IS satisfied in substance by the second upload run (`upload-wire-2.txt` / `upload-result-2.json`), but the artifact body still carries the contradictory self-description. This is a minor documentation inconsistency, not a security defect — the second run proves replication. | Affected EIDs: E-005

blind_spots: [arkcli] [kimi-k2.7-code] Nested or mixed encodings beyond the two-pass percent-decode loop in _decoded_variants.
[arkcli] [kimi-k2.7-code] Unicode homoglyph/confusable bypasses of the internal marker filter beyond NFKC normalization.
[arkcli] [kimi-k2.7-code] URL userinfo credentials and response-body PII retention in replay artifacts.
[arkcli] [kimi-k2.7-code] Multipart filename and header parameter retention in saved replay bodies.
[arkcli] [kimi-k2.7-code] Non-Bash tool paths and direct library calls that bypass safety_gate.py.
[arkcli] [kimi-k2.7-code] Local path patterns outside /Users/ /home, such as /root, /opt, or Windows UNC paths, not matched by _LOCAL_PATH_RE.
[arkcli] [kimi-k2.7-code] Coverage of tools/exploit.py and client_graybox.py for outbound privacy validation.

[claude] **Proxy path entirely unverified**: CLAUDE.md declares `XUNJI_PROXY` as the production default with proxy fail-closed behavior. Every guarded tool (`probe.py`, `render.py`, `scan.py`, `sensors/upload_probe.py`) reads `XUNJI_PROXY` or `tools/harness/proxy.conf`. But zero artifacts exercise the privacy guard through the proxy. A proxy that rewrites URLs (e.g., adding path prefixes, normalizing query parameters), injects tracing headers, or modifies multipart boundary formatting could present bytes to the guard that differ from what loopback tests cover. The proxy trust-boundary documentation in the disposition is necessary but not sufficient — a single proxy-path smoke test with a real SOCKS5/HTTP proxy would resolve this.

[claude] **False-positive behavior under realistic target data is completely untested**: All selftests use synthetic payloads (literal "xunji-proof", "13800138000", etc.). No test sends a legitimate payload that coincidentally matches a deny pattern to verify the guard permits it or provides a clear operator workflow. For example: a JSON body `{"user_dir": "/Users/admin/config"}` would match `_LOCAL_PATH_RE` and be blocked even if it's legitimate target API content. The only documented escape is "author-and-handoff" which is heavyweight for a false positive.

[claude] **`_INTERNAL_PATTERNS` word-boundary semantics are path-naive**: The pattern `\bxunji(?:[_-][a-z0-9._-]+)?\b` uses `\b` which matches at word/non-word boundaries. But `/` is a non-word character, so `https://target.com/api/xunji_status` matches (`xunji` between `/` and `_`). The `_LOCAL_PATH_RE` pattern `(?:^|[\\/])\.claude(?:[\\/]|$)` is path-aware, but the project-identifier pattern is not. A legitimate target endpoint named `xunji-api` or `xunji_status` would be blocked.

[claude] **No evidence that `OUTBOUND_PRIVACY_DENY_VALUES` works correctly**: The environment variable is parsed by `_configured_sensitive_values()` and checked against every candidate. But no test exercises this path with real operator/org identifiers. The guard reports only the category ("configured or local identity value"), never the matched value — this is correct for privacy but means the operator cannot distinguish "my org name matched" from "my home directory matched" during debugging. A dry-run or audit-only mode would help.

[claude] **Encoding bypass: 32-token base64/hex limit is an untested boundary condition**: `_decoded_variants` limits base64 and hex candidate token detection to 32 tokens each. A crafted payload with exactly 33 base64-like strings where the 33rd encodes a project marker would bypass detection. This is low practical risk (exploit payloads rarely contain 32+ base64 tokens) but the boundary is untested and undocumented.

[claude] **No negative multipart test**: E-005 is pure happy-path (neutral upload with no project identifiers). There is no confirmed artifact showing that a multipart upload with a project-labeled filename (`xunji-proof.txt`), field name (`xunji_marker`), or boundary (`----xunji-...`) is actually rejected before I/O. The privacy.py code DOES enforce this (via `validate_outbound_request` checking filenames and the multipart boundary being checked), but the confirmed evidence only shows the allowed path.

[claude] **Redirect body content leakage untested**: E-006 confirms that Cookie and Authorization headers are stripped across origins, but redirect response bodies (e.g., a 302 with HTML body containing session tokens or PII in JavaScript redirects) are not tested. Similarly, redirect target URL query parameters carrying auth data are not tested.
